courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: First Year Seminar: The Migratory Experience
courses.description: The seminar will critically analyze the migrant experience in both North America and Europe. Migration is a calculated decision that individuals, families, and groups make in an effort to improve their living conditions. We will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to understanding the motivation of migrants, the nature of the migrant journey to their destination states, and their integration into their new societies.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Beg, Borrow, and Steal: The Political Economy of Aid, FDI, and Corruption
courses.description: This seminar examines how politics and economics condition different countries' path towards and experience with foreign aid, foreign investment, and corruption. In doing so, the course will examine the effect of political conditions on economic outcomes and the effect of economic conditions on political outcomes.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester. Honors version available.

courses.title: Global Studies Internship

courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Independent Study

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Global Issues and Globalization
courses.description: Survey of international social, political, and cultural patterns in selected societies of Africa, Asia, America, and Europe, stressing comparative analysis of conflicts and change in different historical contexts. LAC recitation sections offered in French, German, and Spanish.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Taiwan, Xinjiang, Hong Kong, and China
courses.description: Taiwan, Hong Kong and Xinjiang represent three different challenges to the objective of national unification or unity championed by Xi Jinping, the current President of the People's Republic of China (PRC). In this class we will explore how the past, present and future of these three different cases might affect not only Xi's ''Chinese Dream'' and the trajectory of the People's Republic, but also global affairs and our understanding of political subjectivity, identity, and nation-building.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Phillips Ambassadors Program
courses.description: This academic course is mandatory for Phillips Ambassadors. Course open only to Phillips Ambassadors.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Global Gap Year Seminar
courses.description: This course is mandatory for Global Gap Year Fellows and is only open to Global Gap Year Fellows.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: History, Memory, and Social Movements
courses.description: This course analyzes the relationships between history, memory, and social movements, using selected episodes from the recent histories of Taiwan and China as primary examples, but also putting them in conversation with histories of other places within a global context whenever possible.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Current Topics in Global Studies
courses.description: An interdisciplinary approach to the study of the background, current status, and future prospects for one of a series of global issues such as the nuclear age, the environment, technological transition.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Special Topics in Global Studies, FC-GLOBAL
courses.description: Topics vary from semester to semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Apology, Forgiveness, and Reconciliation - The Case of Northern Ireland
courses.description: The course, which will take place in Belfast, Northern Ireland, aims to answer the following question: What does it take for an individual and a group to heal? And what does reconciliation mean and look like? The platform of Northern Ireland's conflict (aka ''The Trouble'') will be used to understand the challenges and successes of healing on an individual and group level. The course will provide a nuanced understanding of apology and forgiveness.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Global Research in Practice
courses.description: This survey course introduces students to major global challenges facing policymakers and societies around the world by examining them through multiple disciplinary perspectives and methodological approaches. The course emphasizes interdisciplinary inquiry and exposes students to diverse research strategies in order to broaden their analytical frameworks. A central element of the class is helping students understand and evaluate the research process through the careful analysis of scholarly articles. Students will learn how to dissect academic studies by identifying core theoretical arguments, formulating and evaluating hypotheses, assessing how variables are conceptualized and measured, examining methodological choices, and interpreting empirical findings.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Peacemaking within Alaska - Challenges to Apology, Forgiveness and Reconciliation
courses.description: This course at the University of Alaska in Fairbanks (UAF) aims to provide students with the tools to understand their own relationship with apology, forgiveness, and reconciliation through the lens of Alaska Natives. To achieve this, students will learn about the struggles of Alaska Natives seeking recognition for their suffering and working to forgive and reconcile with Alaska's state government, the U.S. federal government, and business communities who have impacted their livelihood, education, access to natural resources, and culture.

source.text: GLBL 320. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | PWAD 320 , PLCY 320 .

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Great Decisions
courses.description: Eight evening guest lectures, with a discussion session after each, on eight issues in current foreign policy. May be repeated for credit. Students may not receive credit for both GLBL 381 and POLI 381 .
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Latin American Migrant Perspectives: Ethnography and Action
courses.description: This class combines fieldwork, oral history, and service learning in a course that examines concepts of globalization, migration, and transnationalism, and their intersections with anthropological theory and practice.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Global Whiteness
courses.description: This course looks at race as a theory and practice as it has been constructed in academic disciplines, popular culture, and social struggle.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Current Topics in Global Studies
courses.description: Topics vary from semester to semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Teaching Great Decisions II
courses.description: This course links the Great Decisions lecture series with readings and analyses of international relations. Its purpose is to provide the students on the Great Decisions coordinating committee with a practical and intellectual engagement with United States foreign policy and global issues.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 3 total completions.

source.text: GLBL 394. | 2 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, GLBL 381 .

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Special Topics in Global Studies, FC-POWER
courses.description: Topics vary from semester to semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Right Wing Populism in Global Perspective
courses.description: This course will examine right wing populism globally. We will consider why right wing populism has gained traction in such diverse places as India, Brazil, Germany, France, Hungary, Britain, and the United States. We will ask what role such factors as religion, ethnicity, economics, and gender play in its rise. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Socialist and Decolonial Ecologies
courses.description: This course will focus on the relation of capitalism and anthropogenic climate change and feature Marxist and Indigenous critiques of capitalism's responsibility for climate change. We will feature an interdisciplinary lens - philosophy, feminist geography, cultural anthropology, socialist economics - that will analyze how the anthropocentric subject of the Enlightenment separated itself from its natural environment.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Dealing with Difference: Criminal Justice, Race, and Social Movements in Globalization
courses.description: This course is dedicated to understanding how sameness and difference are used and contested globally, in particular through the criminal justice system and its intersection with race and capitalism. The course pays particular attention to popular social movement responses, and what they say to theories of difference, globalization, and social change. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Love and Liberation: Spirituality and Social Change, a Global Perspective
courses.description: Recommended preparation, GLBL 210. This course seeks to explore the intersections of love and freedom and will toggle between the ways in which these ideas are used by activist groups and the spiritual/religious perspectives themselves. There will be a particular emphasis on coming to understand how diverse religious/spiritual perspectives address key problematics or issues such as hierarchy, difference, power, oppression, equality, money, and liberation. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Social Change in Times of Crisis: Knowledge, Action, and Ontology
courses.description: Examines dominant, alternative, and emergent narratives of change and the future from around the world. Takes as a premise that we live in a period of multidimensional crises characterized by uncertainty and conflict about how to pursue sustainable economic, ecological, political, social, and cultural projects. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: NGO Politics
courses.description: This course will investigate how nongovernmental organizations emerge, how they structure their organizations, how they function, and how they influence public policy. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Soviet and Post-Soviet Politics and Institutions
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the history and contemporary politics of the post-Soviet region and explores topics of religious, ethnic, and identity politics; international influences; and civil society and social movements. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Comparative Health Systems
courses.description: This course provides students with an understanding of the origins and comparative performance of a range of international healthcare systems. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: History and Politics of Central Asia
courses.description: This course is an introduction of the history, politics, and societies of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. The class explores the foundations and conditions of change in the modern history of these societies and investigates how these issues influence contemporary politics.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Comparative Development
courses.description: This course is an APPLES service-learning course whose goal is to integrate real-world experience working with development-oriented organizations, theoretical discussions about the origins and evolution of development thinking, and exposure to the challenges facing practitioners of development, in some of its many substantive and geographical contexts.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Sports and Globalization
courses.description: This course explores some of the relationships between sports and globalization and will delve into sports as an important social and cultural practice within larger social, cultural, and political forces shaping studies of globalization. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Social Movements: Rethinking Globalization
courses.description: This course explores the history, objectives, and manifestations of global social movements. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Paradigms of Development and Social Change
courses.description: By deliberately juxtaposing questions of global development with an investigation of approaches in community organizing locally--both through course material and service-learning assignments--the course encourages students to develop a more critical understanding of the relationship between development projects and emancipatory frameworks. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Current Topics
courses.description: Current topics in international and area studies. Topics vary by semester.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Major Controversies in Human Rights
courses.description: A forum for exploring conceptual and practical problems related to the emergence of a global human rights regime after World War II. The course analyzes relevant arguments, and students will consider whether it is possible to construct a coherent, workable, universally accepted system for articulating and enforcing human rights norms.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Global Food Films
courses.description: Thinking about one of our most basic human needs illuminates aspects of our own everyday lives, such as our relationship to nature, other cultures, and to history, as well as our general assumptions about humanity. Students will study films that explore cross-cultural differences in the social and philosophical understandings of what it is to be human. Honors version available.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Political Economy of Poverty and Inequality
courses.description: Introduces students to the political economy of poverty alleviation programs. Uses comparative cases to explore what types of projects, tasks, and environments lead to effective and equitable outcomes, and why.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Honors in Global Studies
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Preparation for writing the honors thesis.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Honors in Global Studies
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Completion of the honors thesis and an oral examination of the thesis.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Introduction to Research and Theory in Global Studies
courses.description: Global studies examines world systems, transnational processes, and global-local interactions from a multi-disciplinary perspective. This course will introduce students to current interdisciplinary theoretical approaches to global studies and examine the primary topics of contemporary research relating to the rise of a complex but increasingly integrated world society.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Political Economy of Development
courses.description: Presents foundational theories, concepts, and empirical research regarding the political economy of development. In content, course will define this topic broadly, from considering the political and economic dynamics of the international community (e.g., aid) as well as the intersection of economics and politics in comparative perspective (e.g., democratization and development).

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Global Politics, Institutions, and Societies
courses.description: This course will address global governance and global public policy; interactions among states, international organizations, businesses, social movements, and NGOs. It addresses the diffusion and promotion of democracy and other norms and the interactions between political institutions and social cleavages. Students with this concentration must take one appropriate methodology class.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Global Migration and Labor Rights
courses.description: The course will focus on the interactions of migration, labor rights, human rights, economics, health disparities, and cross-border tensions. Students with this concentration will also take at least one appropriate disciplinary methodology class.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: The Theory and Practice of Conflict Transformation
courses.description: This course focuses on several mechanisms and strategies for managing and transforming conflict on international, community, and interpersonal levels. We will discuss, in particular, the theory and practice of restorative justice, negotiation, conflict transformation in the digital age, decolonization, and facilitating dialogue and engage in practical exercises in managing conflicts.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Monitoring and Evaluation for Peacebuilding Interventions
courses.description: This introductory course offers a review of the core concepts, skills and practical steps in monitoring and evaluation of coexistence and peacebuilding interventions. The course will stress participatory methods in monitoring and evaluation, in which multiple stakeholders are involved in the process of planning, collecting, interpreting, synthesizing, and using information. The course will feature case studies, proposals, and organizational evaluation plans and reports.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Identities and Transitions
courses.description: Capstone course for the REEES concentration in the Global Studies MA program. Interdisciplinary course focusing on the variety of problems encountered by the societies of East European countries and successor states of the former Soviet Union in their transition from communism to democracy.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Methods for Social Sciences and Policy Research
courses.description: This course presents an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research methods. It addresses the theoretical, ethical, and practical aspects of conducting research in local and global contexts. Students will learn how to collect and analyze empirical information from multiple sources such as interviews, focus groups, written records, and surveys. Students will develop the skills necessary to understand and critique the methods of evaluation in others' work.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Special Topics in Global Studies
courses.description: Instructors and topics vary from semester to semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Global Studies Internship and Field Experience
courses.description: Students may earn academic credit toward degree requirements for completion of an internship or other field experience. Internship and work load must be approved by the Director of Graduate Studies. Specific guidelines must be followed earn academic credit.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Independent Reading and Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Reading and research on special topics in global studies.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: GLBL
courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.description: Master's thesis substitute paper; permission of the instructor required.
